item.title: Labour council looks for caring adults to help young people leaving care
item.description:
Labour council looks for caring adults to help young people leaving care
Swansea's Labour council wants to make sure no young person leaving care has to face adult life on their own. It is looking for caring, compassionate local people to give them steady support through Shared Lives.
Leaving care can be a daunting time. Many young people are still building their confidence while learning to manage adult life, and having a trusted adult alongside them can change a great deal.
Shared Lives gives care leavers the chance to learn practical skills for everyday life, grow in confidence and get consistent support as they move on. The people taking part offer guidance, encouragement and stability at a key moment.
The scheme is run as West Glamorgan Shared Lives, with Swansea Council and Neath Port Talbot Council. Anyone who thinks they could help can email westglamorgansharedlives@npt.gov.uk or call 01639 686123.
Full story at swansealabour.org/news

item.title: Thousands brave the rain as Labour council's Christmas Parade lights up Swansea
item.description:
Thousands brave the rain as Labour council's Christmas Parade lights up Swansea
Swansea's Labour council gave the city a bright start to Christmas on Sunday, when thousands of people filled the city centre streets for the annual Christmas Parade. It rained, and the crowds came anyway.
Local people were at the heart of it. More than 40 local groups joined the procession, among them Rising Stars Theatre Group, Loughor Town Band and Mellin Theatre Arts. Bonymaen Kids Play Initiative was there too, marking its 14th year in the parade.
Labour Leader of Swansea Council, Cllr Rob Stewart, said: "Swansea truly came alive as thousands of people lined the streets for our spectacular Christmas Parade. It's one of the highlights of the festive calendar and I'm incredibly proud of the dedication, creativity and hard work that makes it such a success year after year."
The evening started at the Guildhall, where Santa turned the building a festive red and fireworks followed. There was entertainment on the Guildhall stage, which was supported by Specsavers (Swansea and Mumbles), before the award-winning parade set off.
Marching bands, festive characters and illuminated floats then made their way through the city. The Grinch and Witches of Oz floats were among the highlights, along with Spark! The Light Up Band, Winter Wonderland Birds and Space Cadets. The Land Rider had a seasonal makeover as well. With support from Childcare Offer for Wales, it became the Christmas Train.
There was live entertainment from Reagan Preece, a contestant on The Voice, from Victorian carollers and from the cast of Snow White at Swansea Grand Theatre. Santa finished the night by switching on the city centre Christmas lights and the Christmas tree, and a second fireworks display followed.
Full story at swansealabour.org/news
#Swansea #SwanseaLabour #BuildingABetterSwansea #Castle #Christmas

item.title: Labour council's Christmas Parade is this Sunday: what you need to know
item.description:
Labour council's Christmas Parade is this Sunday: what you need to know
Swansea's Labour council opens the festive season this Sunday, 22 November, with the city's Christmas Parade. Tens of thousands of people are expected, so here is what families need to know before they set off.
The fun begins before Santa appears. Entertainment starts at the Guildhall from 4pm and on the city centre stage from 4.15pm. Santa leaves the Guildhall at 5pm. The two entertainment stages are supported by Specsavers Swansea and Mumbles and will have live music, performances and family entertainment.
Labour Leader of Swansea Council, Cllr Rob Stewart, said: "The Swansea Christmas Parade is one of the highlights of the city's events calendar and it's fantastic to see so many community groups, performers and volunteers taking part, alongside a very special guest, Santa himself."
Getting there need not cost anything. The Labour council's free buses run all day on Sunday for journeys that start and finish within the Swansea Council area, and where services operate after 7pm they stay free until 9pm. Drivers can use extra parking at the Recreation Ground and Civic Centre West for £5 per vehicle. East Burrows and the usual city centre car parks are open too. The Fabian Way Park and Ride will not operate for this year's parade.
Cllr Stewart added: "The return of free bus travel makes it even easier for people to get to the parade, while additional parking will also be available."
The council has set aside space for people who need a calmer view. There are quiet and accessible viewing areas at the Guildhall and at the St Helen's Road end of The Kingsway, and nobody needs to book. Another quieter viewing area is halfway along St Helen's Road. The whole route will still have music, flashing lights and special effects.
Full story at swansealabour.org/news
#Swansea #SwanseaLabour #BuildingABetterSwansea #Castle #Christmas

item.title: Labour council asks residents for their views, with £50 vouchers to be won
item.description:
Labour council asks residents for their views, with £50 vouchers to be won
Swansea's Labour council is asking residents to say what they think about life in the city, and taking part brings the chance to win a £50 shopping voucher.
The council launched its latest appeal by answering a familiar complaint: that the city centre has no shops. Its reply is that the city centre has more than 200 retailers, an award-winning market, more than 150 hospitality businesses and 24 entertainment, culture and attraction venues. Now it wants residents to have their say.
The survey is called Let's Talk: Living in Swansea. It asks what is important to you, what your experience of your local area is, and how you view and deal with the council. It takes about 10 minutes and must be completed by 11.59pm on 6 December 2026.
Everyone who takes part can enter a free prize draw, with five £50 Love2Shop vouchers to be won. The survey is at swansea.gov.uk/residentssurvey, where Word and easy read versions are also available. The Welsh Local Government Association is running it on the council's behalf.
Decisions about Swansea to start with the people who live here. The more residents who reply, the clearer the picture the Labour council has of what matters in each community.
Full story at swansealabour.org/news
#Swansea #SwanseaLabour #BuildingABetterSwansea #HaveYourSay

item.title: Labour welcomes new Men's Shed at Dyfatty Junction community hub
item.description:
Labour welcomes new Men's Shed at Dyfatty Junction community hub
Men in Swansea who have been through probation, prison or substance services have a new place to find company and support, with the launch of a Men's Shed at Dyfatty Junction. Swansea's Labour council is working with the project and has shared news of the launch.
The Common Ground Shed meets every Tuesday from 2pm to 3pm. It gives men the chance to connect, chat and get support, and the sessions are run by mentors who have lived experience themselves. It is free and there is no need to book. Men can simply drop in.
Sessions are held at Dyfatty Junction, the community hub at the top of High Street. The hub opened in June, and Labour Leader of Swansea Council, Cllr Rob Stewart, has said it is already proving a real success.
The new Shed joins a growing movement in the city. Earlier this month the Labour council awarded £40,000 to 23 Men's Sheds and similar community groups across Swansea, and it has invested £175,000 in Men's Sheds over the past seven years.
A friendly, free space for men who might otherwise struggle alone shows Labour's priorities for Swansea: stronger communities, second chances and support close to home.
Full story at swansealabour.org/news
#Swansea #SwanseaLabour #BuildingABetterSwansea #Castle #CommunitySupport

item.title: Labour council buys former TSB building for new young people's hub on The Kingsway
item.description:
Labour council buys former TSB building for new young people's hub on The Kingsway
Young people and families in Swansea are set to get a major new city centre hub, after the Labour council bought the former TSB building on The Kingsway.
The four-storey building at 29-30 The Kingsway is planned to house a range of services in one place. The aim is to make advice, guidance and support easier for young people to reach, in better surroundings.
Labour Leader of Swansea Council, Cllr Rob Stewart, said: "Buying this building gives us a fantastic opportunity to create something really special for Swansea's young people.
"We want somewhere welcoming and accessible where young people can simply walk through the door, as well as a place where a wide range of organisations can work together to provide the support children, young people and families need.
"The former TSB building has huge potential and its city centre location means we can bring services that are currently spread across Swansea together in one place."
Under the plans, the council's Youth Justice Service would move in, together with the services now based at Info-Nation and young people's services that currently run from other sites in Swansea. The ambition is a welcoming "no wrong door" approach, so a young person can reach support from different services in one place.
The ground floor would be an open-access space for young people to drop in. Other floors could hold specialist services, rooms for consultation and assessment, family support and partner organisations. There is also scope for music and creative facilities, therapeutic support, space for workshops and training, and activities for health and wellbeing.
Cabinet members and the chairs of the relevant committees toured the building this week. The Labour administration will work with partners, including third-sector organisations, to draw up proposals for the hub and decide which services could move in. Cllr Stewart added: "We'll now continue working with young people, our partners and the third sector to help shape those plans."

item.title: Labour sets out 10-year vision for greener, safer parks across Swansea
item.description:
Labour sets out 10-year vision for greener, safer parks across Swansea
Families across Swansea can look forward to parks that are greener, safer and more enjoyable to visit, under a new 10-year vision agreed by the city's Labour council.
Cabinet approved the Parks Development Strategy on November 18. It covers the 149 parks the council manages, from Singleton Park and Clyne Gardens to the green spaces in the middle of local communities. It builds on a strong record: more than £11m has already been invested in play areas and in skate and wheeled sports facilities.
Labour's Cabinet Member for Environment and Infrastructure, Cllr Andrew Stevens, said: "Parks can make a huge difference to everyday life. They give children somewhere to play, help people stay active, bring communities together and give all of us space to enjoy nature.
"We've already invested millions of pounds in improving facilities across Swansea, including our hugely-popular £8m play areas programme."
The strategy sets out opportunities for improved paths, lighting, seating and toilets, and for parks that are easier for everyone to get around. It wants parks to be more welcoming for teenagers, including spaces designed with teenage girls. Another key action is to use the National Exercise Referral Scheme to get more people active outdoors in parks and open spaces. Nature is central to the vision. It highlights tree planting, wildflower areas, better habitats and managing parks in a wildlife-friendly way, along with steps to help them deal with climate change and flooding. Communities would be encouraged to take a bigger part through park friends' groups, both existing and new.
Residents helped shape the plan. It was informed by 548 responses to a public survey, 27 stakeholder groups and 112 school pupils. Their priorities included maintenance, toilets, seating, accessibility, safety, facilities for teenagers and protecting nature.
Cllr Stevens added: "People have told us they want parks that are safer, greener, more accessible and welcoming to everybody.
Full story at swansealabour.org/news
#Swansea #SwanseaLabour #BuildingABetterSwansea #Parks

item.title: Labour's free buses are back this weekend: parade road closures to know
item.description:
Labour's free buses are back this weekend: parade road closures to know
Families can get into Swansea city centre by bus without paying a penny this weekend, thanks to Swansea's Labour council. Free buses are back on Saturday 21 and Sunday 22 November, just in time for the Christmas Parade.
The rules are the same as before: a journey is free if it starts and finishes within Swansea. On parade night, any services running after 7pm stay free until 9pm.
Labour Leader of Swansea Council, Cllr Rob Stewart, said: "Swansea is the only council in Wales to offer this opportunity to take the bus and save money in the countdown to Christmas." He added: "Offering free buses to get to and from the Christmas parade is a brilliant early festive present for local families on what will be a great curtain-raiser for the countdown."
The parade is on Sunday 22 November. It starts at 5pm at the Guildhall and is expected to finish at about 6.30pm. The route runs along St Helen's Road and The Kingsway, then College Street, Castle Street and Caer Street, and ends on Princess Way. The city centre is expected to be very busy all afternoon, so allow plenty of time.
Some roads will be closed on Sunday. Guildhall Road North and Francis Street are closed from 8am to 10pm, and Bellevue Way from 12 noon to 9pm. Rolling closures apply from 4pm to 8pm on Guildhall Road South, St Helen's Road, St Helen's Crescent, Christina Street, The Kingsway, Orchard Street, Dillwyn Street, Castle Street, College Street, Caer Street, Castle Bailey Street, Princess Way, and Victoria Road and Oystermouth Road.
Parking is restricted too. From 8am to 10pm there is no parking on Guildhall Road North, Francis Street, the Guildhall Rotunda and The Baths car park. From 2pm to 8pm restrictions apply on St Helen's Road, St Helen's Crescent, The Kingsway, College Street, Castle Street and Princess Way. Drivers can park at the Recreation Ground to watch the start at the Guildhall, or avoid the closures completely by parking at the Civic Centre. A full list of city centre car parks is at swansea.gov.uk/carparks.
Full story at swansealabour.org/news
#Swansea #SwanseaLabour #BuildingABetterSwansea #Castle #Buses

item.title: Hannah Laing to play Singleton Park as Labour's Swansea lines up summer 2027
item.description:
Hannah Laing to play Singleton Park as Labour's Swansea lines up summer 2027
Music fans in Swansea have another big date for 2027. Scottish DJ Hannah Laing will play Singleton Park on Saturday 21 August 2027, in news shared this week by Swansea's Labour-run council.
Laing has built her name on fast-paced sets that draw on trance, techno and hard dance. The poster for the show says the full line-up is still to be announced.
Fans who want the first chance of a ticket can sign up for the presale at visitswanseabay.com/signup. The presale opens at 10am on Wednesday 25 November 2026. Any tickets left go on general sale at 10am on Thursday 26 November.
The show joins a growing list of events already announced for next year. Becky Hill headlines Tunes on the Bay on Swansea Bay Beach on Friday 30 April 2027, and the free Wales Airshow returns on 24 and 25 July 2027.
Labour wants Swansea to be a city with plenty to do, where big nights out are on residents' doorsteps and visitors spend their money with local businesses. A busy 2027 calendar shows the Labour council's work to make Swansea a place people want to come to.

item.title: Labour backs 30 affordable homes at Swansea's historic Castle Cinema
item.description:
Labour backs 30 affordable homes at Swansea's historic Castle Cinema
Thirty affordable homes are on the way in the heart of Swansea, as the Labour council backs the restoration of the city's historic Castle Cinema building.
Construction and restoration work is continuing at the building, which is being converted into 30 affordable apartments. There will also be small office units fronting The Strand, and a two-storey café or restaurant unit with a glazed box looking out over Worcester Place and Castle Square Gardens.
The scheme is led by Beacon Cymru Group and Easy Living Ltd. Swansea's Labour council is supporting it with funding, alongside the Welsh Government. The work is expected to be complete in 2028.
It sits next to another Labour project. Castle Square Gardens is also being redeveloped and is on course to open next summer. Laserzone, which used to be based in the cinema building, has moved to St David's Place.
Local Labour councillor for Castle, Cllr Patience Bentu, said: “Affordable homes in the city centre are badly needed. It is wonderful that 30 of them will be in a building so many people remember fondly.”
Fellow Castle Labour councillor Cllr Fiona Gordon added: “The old Castle Cinema is part of Swansea's story. I am glad to see it being restored and given a new use.”
Fellow Castle Labour councillor Cllr Hannah Lawson added: “Homes, offices and a new café or restaurant facing Castle Square Gardens will bring this corner of our ward back to life.”
Fellow Castle Labour councillor Cllr David Phillips added: “More people living in the city centre is good for our shops and businesses. This scheme helps to make that happen.”
Bringing a historic building back into use, with homes people can afford, is what Labour wants for the city centre: heritage looked after and more people living at its heart.
Full story at swansealabour.org/news
#Swansea #SwanseaLabour #BuildingABetterSwansea #Castle #Housing

item.title: Labour's Castle Square Gardens on course to open next summer
item.description:
Labour's Castle Square Gardens on course to open next summer
Swansea's new-look Castle Square Gardens is on course to open next summer, as Labour's transformation of the city centre square moves forward.
Labour Leader of Swansea Council, Cllr Rob Stewart, went to the site this week with fellow cabinet members. They saw how far the work has come and heard the latest from main contractor Knights Brown.
Cllr Stewart said: "It's great to see the impressive progress being made. This is a complex project in a busy city-centre location, so I'm delighted it remains on target for opening next summer.
"The new-look Castle Square Gardens will create a fantastic space that people can enjoy for many years."
When it opens, the square will be a greener and more welcoming place in the heart of the city. It will have significantly more landscaping and new seating, with better facilities for events and for everyday use.
On site, drainage work has been carried out and the frames and roof structures are being built for the new commercial units. Each unit will have a green roof. The council is looking for ambitious café, restaurant and hospitality operators to move into them. Across the rest of the site, work continues towards new greenery, paving and granite planters.
Knights Brown said it was pleased with progress and was working closely with the council to deliver the project.
Residents can hear more at a community event on 26 November, from 2.30pm to 4.30pm, at Y Storfa on Oxford Street. The council's project team and Knights Brown will be there.
Local Labour councillor for Castle, Cllr Patience Bentu, said: “It is exciting to see the new Castle Square Gardens taking shape. A greener square with more seating will be a real asset for everyone who lives in and visits the city centre.”
Fellow Castle Labour councillor Cllr Fiona Gordon added: “New cafés and restaurants with green roofs will bring more life to the square. I am pleased the work is on target for next summer.”
Full story at swansealabour.org/news

item.title: Labour welcomes first gondola tower for Swansea's Kilvey Hill cable car
item.description:
Labour welcomes first gondola tower for Swansea's Kilvey Hill cable car
The first gondola tower for Swansea's new cable car is now standing at the base of Kilvey Hill, and Labour council leader Cllr Rob Stewart has welcomed the progress.
Skyline, the company behind the attraction, said the tower was another milestone for the project.
Work on the lower station is moving quickly too. Its steel frame is going up and the bullwheel has been lifted into place. In October, Swansea's Labour council welcomed the start of that steelwork at Landore, after the base station's foundations were completed.
From there, the line will run up Kilvey Hill to the summit, where visitors will be able to look out across Swansea Bay.
Sharing the news, Labour Leader of Swansea Council, Cllr Rob Stewart, said: "Another fantastic regeneration project making great progress in our City"
Labour is backing projects like this because they bring visitors to Swansea, create new opportunities and give the city something to be proud of.

item.title: Labour council confirms free Wales Airshow returns on 24 and 25 July 2027
item.description:
Labour council confirms free Wales Airshow returns on 24 and 25 July 2027
Wales' largest free event is coming back. Swansea's Labour council has confirmed that the Wales Airshow will return to Swansea on 24 and 25 July 2027.
The award-winning show draws more than 200,000 visitors each year, with families and aviation fans travelling from across the UK.
Labour's Cabinet Member for Development, Cllr Andrew Williams, said: "We are delighted to confirm the return of the Wales Airshow in 2027. It's a major feature of the summer season and brings thousands of visitors to Swansea each year."
Over the two days, a variety of aircraft will fly displays above the five-mile sweep of Swansea Bay. On the ground there will be fairground rides, live music, exhibitors, family entertainment, and food and drink.
The last show ended with Afterburn, an evening programme of flying displays, a display by two hundred drones celebrating Welsh culture, and a fireworks finale. The Labour council is now looking at bringing it back.
Cllr Williams said: "Our teams are already working on their plans for next year and that includes looking at proposals for a return of the hugely successful Afterburn show. And, of course, an there will be an invite to the Red Arrows after they missed last year due to commitments in the United States.
"We know how much the Red Arrows love the Swansea crowds, so we're hopeful we'll be on their list when they reveal their plans next year."
The full flying programme and more entertainment will be announced nearer the time. Updates will be posted at www.walesairshow.com and by @walesairshow on Facebook and Instagram.
A free event on this scale brings visitors and trade to the city, and gives local families a great weekend out. Labour is keeping it at the heart of Swansea's summer.
Full story at swansealabour.org/news
#Swansea #SwanseaLabour #BuildingABetterSwansea #WhatsOn

item.title: Labour council lines up weeks of festive family fun for Swansea city centre
item.description:
Labour council lines up weeks of festive family fun for Swansea city centre
Swansea's Labour council has lined up a packed Christmas programme for the city centre, giving families somewhere to go and something to do from this week right through the festive season.
It starts on 19 November, when Winter Wonderland opens at Museum Green. Visitors can skate on the ice, ride the big wheel and the fairground rides, and stop for food and drink.
The city centre's Christmas Market follows on 21 November. The Christmas Parade and Lights Switch On come a day later, on 22 November. Mistletoe & Markets is on 28 November, and the Fire & Ice Festival is back on 5 December.
Labour Leader of Swansea Council, Cllr Rob Stewart, said: "Christmas is always a special time in Swansea and we want families to have plenty of reasons to come to the city centre and enjoy everything on offer."
There is plenty indoors too, with festive activities for families at cultural attractions such as the Grand Theatre and Glynn Vivian. The Labour council also wants the season to be a good one for local traders. Shops, independent businesses, Swansea Market stallholders, cafés, restaurants and entertainment venues are all ready to welcome visitors.
Getting there will cost less as well, because free bus travel will be on offer at points over the festive period. Labour's free buses run on 21 and 22 November for the parade weekend, on every weekend in the countdown to Christmas, and from 21 to 31 December when buses are operating. More details are at www.visitswanseabay.com.
A busy, welcoming city centre at Christmas is good for families and good for the businesses that depend on it. Labour is making sure Swansea has both, with events for all ages and help with the cost of getting there.
Full story at swansealabour.org/news
#Swansea #SwanseaLabour #BuildingABetterSwansea #Christmas

item.title: St Helen's hosts first international since Labour council-backed redevelopment
item.description:
St Helen's hosts first international since Labour council-backed redevelopment
Swansea rugby fans have watched international rugby at St Helen's for the first time since the historic ground's redevelopment, a project supported by Swansea's Labour council.
Wales U19s took on France U19s there on the evening of Saturday November 14, and staged a comeback to win 34 - 31. It gave supporters the chance to see the international stars of the future on their doorstep.
The redevelopment has given St Helen's a new role as the home of the Ospreys, Swansea RFC and community sport.
Labour Leader of Swansea Council, Cllr Rob Stewart, said: “This is another exciting milestone in the ongoing redevelopment of St Helen’s, which demonstrates the progress being made in securing a bright future for this famous ground. It’s also great to see the Welsh Rugby Union showing confidence in St Helen’s as a venue for international sport.
“We’ve already seen how successfully St Helen’s has embraced its new role as the home of the Ospreys, alongside Swansea RFC and community sport, bringing new energy and excitement to the venue.
“Hosting fixtures like this reinforces our ambition to make St Helen’s a thriving home for rugby at every level, from grassroots and community participation through to the professional and international game.”
Backing a famous ground so it can serve everyone, from local clubs to international sides, shows where Labour's priorities lie: investing in the places Swansea is proud of and making sure communities share in the benefit.

#Swansea #SwanseaLabour #BuildingABetterSwansea #Sport

item.title: Labour council starts Killay flood scheme: what the traffic changes mean
item.description:
Labour council starts Killay flood scheme: what the traffic changes mean
Killay is getting better protection from flooding in severe rainfall, as Swansea's Labour council moves ahead with a major scheme at Killay Square. Drivers will see changes to traffic in the area from Monday 16 November.
From that date, vehicles will not be able to get onto Gower Road from Goetre Fawr Road. Goetre Fawr Road will become one-way between Gower Road and Broadmead, with traffic heading towards Dunvant Road.
Drivers coming from Gowerton or Dunvant to the shops in Killay should use Dunvant Road and Goetre Fach Road. Through traffic should carry on along Dunvant Road and Wimmerfield Drive to reach Sketty or Gower.
The work is expected to take around 25 weeks. Anyone who regularly travels through Killay is asked to allow a little extra time for their journey.
The Labour administration is installing an 'overflow' drainage system at Killay Square, because the existing drains cannot cope with the volume of water in heavy rain. Flooding has repeatedly forced the junction to close. The scheme is funded through the Welsh Government Regional Transport Fund.
Residents who want to know more can call in at Killay Library, where there is more information and a public display about the scheme.
Local Labour councillor for Dunvant & Killay, Cllr Louise Gibbard, said: “We all know what happens at Killay Square when the heavy rain comes, so it is good to see this work under way. Please allow a little extra time for your journey while it is done.”
A few months of changed routes will leave Killay with a junction that stays open when the weather turns. That is Labour's priority for Swansea: fixing long-standing local problems properly, and being straight with residents about what the work involves.
Full story at swansealabour.org/news

item.title: Labour's Copr Bay North car park open as new screens promote Swansea events
item.description:
Labour's Copr Bay North car park open as new screens promote Swansea events
Shoppers and visitors can now use the Copr Bay North car park in Swansea city centre, and new digital screens on its side are telling people what is coming up in the city. Swansea's Labour council has shared the latest progress.
The screens are on the Cupid Way side of the car park. They are now streaming information about upcoming Swansea events. One of the adverts in the council's video is for Singleton Live at Singleton Park in August 2027.
There is good news on the shops too. The council says talks are progressing well with a number of retailers who are interested in taking on the retail units below the car park.
Local Labour councillor for Castle, Cllr Patience Bentu, said: “It is great to see the Copr Bay North car park open and the new screens letting people know what is on in Swansea.”
Fellow Castle Labour councillor Cllr Fiona Gordon added: “Retailers showing interest in the units below the car park is really encouraging news for our city centre.”
Fellow Castle Labour councillor Cllr Hannah Lawson added: “The screens on Cupid Way are a simple way to tell everyone passing by about upcoming Swansea events. I look forward to seeing the retail units filled too.”
Fellow Castle Labour councillor Cllr David Phillips added: “Step by step, this part of the city centre is coming to life. An open car park and talks with retailers going well are both welcome progress.”
Parking that is open, events promoted to everyone passing by and interest from retailers are all signs of a city centre moving forward under Labour. It shows the Labour administration's priority: a busy, welcoming city centre that works for residents and local businesses.

item.title: Labour council brings Pension Credit help to Gorseinon with free drop-in session
item.description:
Labour council brings Pension Credit help to Gorseinon with free drop-in session
Older people in Gorseinon can find out whether they are missing out on Pension Credit, thanks to a drop-in session supported by Swansea's Labour council on 19 November.
The session runs from 9.30am to 12.30pm at Maes Yr Efail, West Street, Gorseinon, SA4 4AE. It is the first in a series of drop-ins the council is supporting over the coming weeks.
Anyone over State Pension age may be eligible to claim. The council's Financial Inclusion Team can help people check what they are entitled to.
A successful claim can unlock much more than the payment itself. It could bring free dental care, free or discounted eye tests and glasses, a Council Tax reduction and help with rent. It can also give access to Winter Fuel Vouchers and the Warm Home Discount Scheme, and a free TV Licence for people over 75.
Local Labour councillor for Gorseinon & Penyrheol, Cllr Andrew Stevens, said: “Too many pensioners miss out on money that is theirs by right. If you or someone you know might qualify, please call in at Maes Yr Efail on 19 November.”
Fellow Gorseinon & Penyrheol Labour councillor Cllr Jan Curtice added: “I am really pleased this session is coming to Gorseinon. Pension Credit can open the door to help with dental care, eye tests and Council Tax, so it is well worth checking.”
Fellow Gorseinon & Penyrheol Labour councillor Cllr Nicola Matthews added: “A quick chat with the Financial Inclusion Team could make a real difference this winter. Please tell older friends, family and neighbours about it.”
Labour councillors want every pensioner to receive the support they are due. Taking this help into the heart of the community is typical of the Labour administration's priorities: putting money back in people's pockets and looking after those who need it most this winter.
Full story at swansealabour.org/news
#Swansea #SwanseaLabour #BuildingABetterSwansea #Gorseinon #CostOfLiving

item.title: Labour invites residents to see progress on new-look Castle Square Gardens
item.description:
Labour invites residents to see progress on new-look Castle Square Gardens
People in Swansea can find out for themselves how the new-look Castle Square Gardens is coming along, at a community engagement event organised by Swansea's Labour council.
The event takes place on 26 November, from 2.30pm to 4.30pm, at Y Storfa, 277-278 Oxford Street, SA1 3EL. Members of the council's project team will be there, along with main contractors Knights Brown, to meet residents and talk about the work.
This will not be the only chance to hear about the scheme. The council says more community engagement events will follow.
Castle Square Gardens is part of the Labour administration's wider investment in Swansea city centre. Once the work is complete, more than 40% of the square will be green space. There will be extra trees and planting, interactive water features, better public spaces, and new places to eat and drink in café and restaurant pavilions. The scheme is due to open in summer 2027.
Work on site has been moving on. In September the council said the steelwork was complete for one of the new pavilion buildings.
Speaking in September, Labour Leader of Swansea Council, Cllr Rob Stewart, said: "People can already see that Castle Square Gardens is starting to take shape."
Local Labour councillor for Castle, Cllr Patience Bentu, said: “Castle Square is right at the heart of our ward, so I'd encourage residents to call in at Y Storfa, meet the team and ask their questions.”
Fellow Castle Labour councillor Cllr Fiona Gordon added: “More than 40% of the new square will be green space. That is a big change for the city centre, and I'm glad people are being invited in to see how it is going.”
Fellow Castle Labour councillor Cllr Hannah Lawson added: “It's good that the project team and the contractors are making time to talk to local people. I hope lots of our residents can come along.”

item.title: Labour council to host new team for North Gate Swansea's £20m Pride in Place programme
item.description:
Labour council to host new team for North Gate Swansea's £20m Pride in Place programme
Communities from Upper High Street to Hafod are getting a dedicated team to help turn local ideas into action. Three people have been appointed to deliver North Gate Swansea's £20 million Pride in Place programme, and Swansea's Labour council will host them.
Alfie joins as full-time Programme Lead, Dawn as full-time Programme Officer and Helen as part-time Programme Officer. They were chosen from 74 applications after a competitive recruitment process.
The programme provides £20 million over 10 years for lasting improvements across Upper High Street, Dyfatty, Hafod, Waun Wen, Brynmelyn, North Hill and surrounding neighbourhoods inside its boundary. It is funded by the UK Government and is designed so that local people are central to decisions about where they live.
The Labour-run council is the programme's accountable body. The staff will take their direction from the Independent Chair, Thom Lynch, and the Neighbourhood Board. Their posts are paid for from the programme's early capacity funding, so the board has dedicated support while it carries on developing its priorities and long-term investment plans.
The new team will begin work on 30 November and 7 December 2026. Their first task is to get out and meet residents, businesses, charities, schools and community organisations. They will also go through the feedback and ideas already collected.
Between them, the three bring experience in project management, community development, youth work, grant management, and supporting children, families and vulnerable people. They have worked in communities across Swansea, including in the North Gate area.
Residents can have their say through the programme's community survey, join its mailing list at northgateswanseapip.co.uk/contact, or email hello@northgateswanseapip.co.uk.
